John F. Street :: Background and early career :: chunk_0001
Street was born in [Norristown, Pennsylvania](/wiki/Norristown,_Pennsylvania "Norristown, Pennsylvania"), and grew up as a member of a farming household. He graduated from Conshohocken High School, received a [B.A.](/wiki/Bachelor_of_Arts "Bachelor of Arts") degree in [English](/wiki/English_language "English language") from [Oakwood College](/wiki/Oakwood_University "Oakwood University") in [Huntsville, Alabama](/wiki/Huntsville,_Alabama "Huntsville, Alabama"), and his [J.D.](/wiki/Juris_Doctor "Juris Doctor") degree from [Temple University](/wiki/Temple_University_Beasley_School_of_Law "Temple University Beasley School of Law"), which he had to apply to several times before he was accepted. Following his graduation from law school, Street served clerkships with Common Pleas Court Judge Mathew W. Bullock, Jr. and with the [United States Department of Justice](/wiki/United_States_Department_of_Justice "United States Department of Justice") from which he was quickly terminated for poor performance. In his first professional job Street taught English at an elementary school and, later, at the Philadelphia [Opportunities Industrialization Center (OIC)](/wiki/Opportunities_Industrialization_Center "Opportunities Industrialization Center"). He then practiced law briefly prior to entering into public service. Street is married and has four children, including [Sharif Street](/wiki/Sharif_Street "Sharif Street"),[[5]](#cite_note-5) and is a practicing [Seventh-day Adventist](/wiki/Seventh-day_Adventist_Church "Seventh-day Adventist Church"). His deceased brother, [Milton](/wiki/T._Milton_Street "T. Milton Street"), was a former member of the [state legislature](/wiki/Pennsylvania_General_Assembly "Pennsylvania General Assembly"), and a two-time [mayoral candidate](/wiki/Mayor_of_Philadelphia,_Pennsylvania "Mayor of Philadelphia, Pennsylvania").

[Saint Louis'](/wiki/Louis_IX_of_France "Louis IX of France") [Sainte-Chapelle](/wiki/Sainte-Chapelle "Sainte-Chapelle") represents the French impact on religious architecture.

During the Middle Ages, many fortified castles were built by feudal nobles to mark their powers. Some French castles that survive are [Chinon](/wiki/Chinon_(castle) "Chinon (castle)"), [Château d'Angers](/wiki/Ch%C3%A2teau_d%27Angers "Château d'Angers"), [Château de Vincennes](/wiki/Ch%C3%A2teau_de_Vincennes "Château de Vincennes") and the [Cathar castles](/wiki/Cathar_castles "Cathar castles"). During this era, France had been using [Romanesque architecture](/wiki/Romanesque_architecture "Romanesque architecture") like most of Western Europe.

[Gothic architecture](/wiki/Gothic_architecture "Gothic architecture"), originally named *Opus Francigenum* meaning "French work",[[311]](#cite_note-323) was born in [Île-de-France](/wiki/%C3%8Ele-de-France "Île-de-France") and was the first French style of architecture to be imitated throughout Europe.[[312]](#cite_note-324) Northern France is the home of some of the most important Gothic cathedrals and basilicas, the first of these being the [Saint Denis Basilica](/wiki/Basilica_of_Saint-Denis "Basilica of Saint-Denis") (used as the royal necropolis); other important French Gothic cathedrals are [Notre-Dame de Chartres](/wiki/Chartres_Cathedral "Chartres Cathedral") and [Notre-Dame d'Amiens](/wiki/Amiens_Cathedral "Amiens Cathedral"). Main article: [Queens High School for the Sciences](/wiki/Queens_High_School_for_the_Sciences "Queens High School for the Sciences")

The Queens High School for the Sciences at York College was formed in 2002 and continued to grow each year as a new class entered, reaching its present size in 2006, when the fifth class was admitted. There are now more than 500 students. As of 2024 the school is #1 in New York State and #25 in the nation, according to *U.S. News & World Report*. The school emphasizes small class sizes and is the only specialized school in Queens.

Despite the filing, during that year the company said that it was not going to move its headquarters.[[198]](#cite_note-198) In 1994, Dell announced that it was moving most of its employees out of the Arboretum, but that it was going to continue to occupy the top floor of the Arboretum and that the company's official headquarters address would continue to be the Arboretum. The top floor continued to hold Dell's board room, demonstration center, and visitor meeting room. Less than one month prior to August 29, 1994, Dell moved 1,100 customer support and telephone sales employees to Round Rock.[[199]](#cite_note-199) Dell's lease in the Arboretum had been scheduled to expire in 1994.[[200]](#cite_note-200)

Scottish botanist [David Don](/wiki/David_Don "David Don") described the redwood as *Taxodium sempervirens*, the "evergreen *[Taxodium](/wiki/Taxodium "Taxodium")*", in his colleague [Aylmer Bourke Lambert](/wiki/Aylmer_Bourke_Lambert "Aylmer Bourke Lambert")'s 1824 work *A description of the genus Pinus*.[[16]](#cite_note-don_1824-16) Austrian botanist [Stephan Endlicher](/wiki/Stephan_Endlicher "Stephan Endlicher") erected the genus *[Sequoia](/wiki/Sequoia_(genus) "Sequoia (genus)")* in his 1847 work *Synopsis coniferarum*, giving the redwood its current binomial name of *Sequoia sempervirens*.[[17]](#cite_note-17) It is unknown how Endlicher derived the name Sequoia. See [*Sequoia* Etymology](/wiki/Sequoia_(genus)#Etymology "Sequoia (genus)").

The redwood is one of three living species, each in its own genus, in the subfamily [Sequoioideae](/wiki/Sequoioideae "Sequoioideae"). Molecular studies have shown that the three are each other's closest relatives, generally with the redwood and giant sequoia (*[Sequoiadendron giganteum](/wiki/Sequoiadendron_giganteum "Sequoiadendron giganteum")*) as each other's closest relatives.

However, Yang and colleagues in 2010 queried the polyploid state of the redwood and speculate that it may have arisen as an ancient [hybrid](/wiki/Hybrid_(biology) "Hybrid (biology)") between ancestors of the giant sequoia and dawn redwood (*[Metasequoia](/wiki/Metasequoia "Metasequoia")*). Using two different single copy [nuclear genes](/wiki/Nuclear_gene "Nuclear gene"), [LFY](/wiki/Leafy "Leafy") and NLY, to generate [phylogenetic trees](/wiki/Phylogenetic_tree "Phylogenetic tree"), they found that *Sequoia* was clustered with *Metasequoia* in the tree generated using the LFY gene, but with *Sequoiadendron* in the tree generated with the NLY gene. [Machine learning](/wiki/Machine_learning "Machine learning") will be used to determine the age of the user (regardless of any account information indicating their age) and restrict access to certain content and features across all Google properties, including YouTube (including, in particular, disabling personalized advertising and enabling certain digital wellbeing limits), if they are assumed to be under 18. On YouTube, this will be based on factors such as searches and video history, and the age of the account. fanoutqa_002843.x:
Big Tech :: Nicknames :: Big Four :: chunk_0011
In the early 2010s, [Alphabet](/wiki/Alphabet_Inc. "Alphabet Inc."), [Amazon](/wiki/Amazon_(company) "Amazon (company)"), [Apple](/wiki/Apple_Inc. "Apple Inc."), and [Meta](/wiki/Meta_Platforms "Meta Platforms") were referred to as the Big Four, The Four, the Gang of Four, and the [Four Horsemen](/wiki/Four_Horsemen_of_the_Apocalypse "Four Horsemen of the Apocalypse").[[80]](#cite_note-80)[[81]](#cite_note-81)[[82]](#cite_note-gang4_schmidt-82) [Eric Schmidt](/wiki/Eric_Schmidt "Eric Schmidt"), [Phil Simon](/wiki/Phil_Simon "Phil Simon"), and [Scott Galloway](/wiki/Scott_Galloway_(professor) "Scott Galloway (professor)") grouped the Big Four together based on their ability to create [social change](/wiki/Social_change "Social change"). They serve billions of users,[[83]](#cite_note-83) and are able to influence user behavior and control large amounts of user data.[[84]](#cite_note-brookings-84) As such, they have been criticized for creating a new economic order called [surveillance capitalism](/wiki/Surveillance_capitalism "Surveillance capitalism").[[85]](#cite_note-85) According to Simon and Galloway, this distinguishes them from other Big Tech companies such as [Microsoft](/wiki/Microsoft "Microsoft") and [IBM](/wiki/IBM "IBM").[[86]](#cite_note-Simon_redefined-86)[[87]](#cite_note-hidden_DNA-87)

In 2011, Google executive chair Eric Schmidt excluded Microsoft from the group, stating, "Microsoft is not driving the consumer revolution in the minds of the consumers."[[88]](#cite_note-88)[[89]](#cite_note-89) In the late 2010s, Microsoft changed its [business strategy](/wiki/Strategic_management "Strategic management"), causing its market value to increase, leading to its widespread inclusion in Big Tech and creating the term Big Five.[[90]](#cite_note-Financial_Times_article_on_MAGA-90)[[73]](#cite_note-cnbc_mamaa-73)[[91]](#cite_note-microsoft-most-valuable-91)

AlphaGo played South Korean professional Go player [Lee Sedol](/wiki/Lee_Sedol "Lee Sedol"), ranked 9-dan, one of the best players at Go,[[16]](#cite_note-CNN0128-16) with five games taking place at the [Four Seasons Hotel](/wiki/Four_Seasons_Hotel "Four Seasons Hotel") in [Seoul](/wiki/Seoul "Seoul"), South Korea on 9, 10, 12, 13, and 15 March 2016,[[24]](#cite_note-24)[[25]](#cite_note-25) which were video-streamed live.[[26]](#cite_note-26) Out of five games, AlphaGo won four games and Lee won the fourth game which made him recorded as the only human player who beat AlphaGo in all of its 74 official games.[[27]](#cite_note-koreatimes_beatable-27) AlphaGo ran on Google's cloud computing with its servers located in the United States.[[28]](#cite_note-JoongAng_Ilbo-28) The match used [Chinese rules](/wiki/Rules_of_go#Chinese_rules "Rules of go") with a 7.5-point [komi](/wiki/Komidashi "Komidashi"), and each side had two hours of thinking time plus three 60-second [byoyomi](/wiki/Byoyomi "Byoyomi") periods.[[29]](#cite_note-Korea_Baduk_Association-29) The version of AlphaGo playing against Lee used a similar amount of computing power as was used in the Fan Hui match.[[30]](#cite_note-30) *[The Economist](/wiki/The_Economist "The Economist")* reported that it used 1,920 [CPUs](/wiki/Central_processing_unit "Central processing unit") and 280 [GPUs](/wiki/Graphics_processing_unit "Graphics processing unit").[[31]](#cite_note-31) At the time of play, Lee Sedol had the second-highest number of Go international championship victories in the world after South Korean player [Lee Chang-ho](/wiki/Lee_Chang-ho "Lee Chang-ho") who kept the world championship title for 16 years.[[32]](#cite_note-32) Since there is no single official method of [ranking in international Go](/wiki/Go_ranks_and_ratings#Rating_systems "Go rank

After the 2004 season, the Athletics traded Mulder to the [St. Louis Cardinals](/wiki/St._Louis_Cardinals "St. Louis Cardinals") in exchange for [Dan Haren](/wiki/Dan_Haren "Dan Haren"), [Kiko Calero](/wiki/Kiko_Calero "Kiko Calero"), and [Daric Barton](/wiki/Daric_Barton "Daric Barton").[[4]](#cite_note-4) In the 2005 season, Mulder's first with the Cardinals, he pitched well, 16–8 with a 3.64 ERA. His efforts helped the Cardinals reach the NLCS, where they lost to the [Houston Astros](/wiki/Houston_Astros "Houston Astros").[[5]](#cite_note-mulder-5)

Mulder began the 2006 season strong, with a 5–1 record and 3.69 ERA through May 17. However, his next six starts were mediocre to awful, and his ERA ballooned to 6.09. He turned out to be suffering from [rotator cuff](/wiki/Rotator_cuff "Rotator cuff") and shoulder problems, and the Cardinals placed him on the disabled list on June 23. In August, he was taken off the disabled list and made several starts in the minors. On August 23, he made his first major-league start in two months and gave up nine runs, all of which were earned, in three innings.

After undergoing rotator cuff surgery, and with a return for the opening of the 2007 season unlikely, Mulder's future with the Cardinals looked somewhat uncertain in the 2007 offseason. However, despite being offered comparable deals with the [Cleveland Indians](/wiki/Cleveland_Indians "Cleveland Indians") and the [Texas Rangers](/wiki/Texas_Rangers_(baseball) "Texas Rangers (baseball)"), Mulder re-signed with the [St. Louis Cardinals](/wiki/St._Louis_Cardinals "St. Louis Cardinals") on January 10, to a two-year $13 million contract, with performance-based incentives and a club option that could take the deal to three years at a possible $45 million.

After being re-activated on September 5, 2007, he continued to struggle with his command, losing all three of his starts with an ERA of 12.27

The **2023 NBA playoffs** was the [postseason tournament](/wiki/NBA_playoffs "NBA playoffs") of the [National Basketball Association](/wiki/National_Basketball_Association "National Basketball Association")'s [2022–23 season](/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_NBA_season "2022–23 NBA season"). The 2023 title was the Nuggets' first title in franchise history.
